descriptionChirho: Intransitive Qal sense: to become slack, feeble, or weak, describing hands, bodies, or resolve losing strength.
Reflexive sense of showing oneself slack or lazy, used of people who are idle or negligent in their duties.
Intensive-causative Piel sense: to actively weaken or discourage someone, undermining their hands or morale.
Piel sense of physically letting something drop or lower, as with ropes or cords.
Hifil causative sense of releasing, letting go of, or leaving someone or something alone; includes desisting from holding.
Hifil sense of failing or abandoning someone, used especially in divine promises of not forsaking.
Hifil sense of ceasing an action, stopping, or withdrawing from activity; overlaps with 'desist' and 'be still.'
Qal sense of sinking or declining, used of the day waning or physical subsiding.
Qal consecutive-imperfect sense of relenting or letting go in narrative sequence, describing a cessation of action.
